name: Eleven v4
access: ElevenLabs API: Text to Speech and Text to Dialogue (HTTP and stream)

voice.input_audio: none: the model takes text, with optional inline audio tags
voice.output_audio: MP3 (22.05 kHz at 32 kbps, 24 kHz at 48 kbps, 44.1 kHz at 32 to 192 kbps), PCM 8 to 48 kHz 16-bit, WAV 8 to 48 kHz, Opus 48 kHz (32 to 192 kbps), mu-law 8 kHz and A-law 8 kHz; the default is mp3_44100_128; MP3 at 192 kbps needs the Creator plan or above, and PCM or WAV at 44.1 kHz needs Pro or above [el-api-tts]
voice.voices: custom cloning: library voices (the maker's pages give 3,000+, 10,000+ and 5,000+ as counts), instant and professional voice clones, and designed voices [el-tts-overview] [el-voices]
languages: 90+ languages; the models page lists them by ISO 639-3 code [el-models]
voice.turn_detection: none: a synthesis model. On the Text to Dialogue WebSocket the client ends a speaker turn with new_turn or by changing voice_id [el-ws-ttd]
voice.interruption: Not a conversation model: the client stops playback. The docs describe no cancel message for the Text to Dialogue WebSocket; flush forces buffered text out and close_socket ends the stream [el-ws-ttd]
voice.latency: The docs state no inference latency for eleven_v4; Artificial Analysis reports a median of 73.5 characters generated per second (throughput, not latency) [aa-tts-board]. The low-latency variant is Eleven v4 Turbo
voice.session_limit: 10,000 characters per request, about 10 minutes of audio [el-models]; the Text to Dialogue page advises at most 2,000 characters per request [el-ttd-overview]; the Text to Dialogue WebSocket closes after 20 seconds without a client message unless keep_alive is sent [el-ws-ttd]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: Per character, not per token. API list price US$0.08 per 1,000 characters; a promotional price of US$0.022 per 1,000 characters (72% off) runs until 2026-10-12 [el-pricing-api]. Artificial Analysis lists US$80 per 1M characters [aa-tts-v4]. Website generation draws credits from the plan; the credit rate for v4 was not found [el-billing]

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Speech Arena Elo (provider voice leaderboard)
benchmarks.setting: blind pairwise listener votes on ElevenLabs's own voices; Artificial Analysis states that v4 currently has the highest quality in its text-to-speech comparison; the leaderboard table read the same day gives the same figure

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis text-to-speech median characters per second
benchmarks.setting: median generation speed; read from the leaderboard data on the Artificial Analysis text-to-speech page

benchmarks.name: Maker blind listening test against four competing speech models
benchmarks.setting: about 75% preference; graders judged expressiveness and naturalness; ties counted as half; competitors were Cartesia Sonic 3.6, Inworld TTS-2, Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS; September 2026; run by the maker

sources.quote: Style and Speed sliders are not available in Eleven v4, and SSML is not supported.
